data.title: Collegium favours a 'particular section' over merit, diversity: Ex-CJI
data.description:
Former Chief Justice of India BR Gavai on Friday wrote to President Droupadi Murmu seeking her intervention in judicial appointments and transfers. He alleged that recent Collegium recommendations favour candidates from "one particular section of the society", at the expense of merit, diversity and inclusivity.
 
In a three-page letter, Gavai alleged that candidates from one section of society were being favoured for elevation to the higher judiciary, while Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), minorities, women and other communities were being excluded.
 
"I am constrained to voice my dissent and disappointment," Gavai wrote, alleging that recent appointments and transfers were being made in disregard of diversity, inclusion and merit.
 
 
The letter was addressed to President Murmu and marked to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal.

Gavai questions representation in higher judiciary

Gavai said a community accounting for less than 5 per cent of India's population had secured more than 40 per cent representation in the Supreme Court in the recent past.
 
He also referred to data presented by Union Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal in the Rajya Sabha in March 2025.
 
According to the data, of the 715 high court judges appointed since 2018, 22 belonged to the Scheduled Castes (SCs), 16 to the Scheduled Tribes (STs), 89 to the Other Backward Classes (OBCs) and 37 to minority communities. Together, these four categories accounted for 164 appointments, or around 23 per cent of the total.
 
Gavai said the representation of different sections of society had been considered during his tenure in the Collegium.
 
In the letter, he wrote: "When I was a part of the collegium and was Chief Justice of India, I always followed the principles of diversity and inclusion."
 
He added that adequate representation was ensured for SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities and women while considering candidates for elevation to the high courts and the Supreme Court.
 
However, he alleged that recent recommendations ignored these principles. "In the recent past disturbing events have unfolded, showing complete disregard for the principles of merit and inclusivity," he wrote.

Gavai questions recent transfers and appointments

The former CJI also raised concerns over the transfer of high court judges and subsequent recommendations for their elevation.
 
He referred to an instance in which a chief justice was transferred from one high court to a smaller high court and was subsequently recommended for appointment as the chief justice of a prominent high court.
 
Gavai alleged that another meritorious and hardworking chief justice was transferred to a smaller high court to accommodate the appointment.
 
He said he had been part of the Collegium that recommended the first chief justice's transfer and later headed the Collegium when the subsequent transfer recommendation was made.
 
"I am aware of the factors that prevailed at the relevant time with the collegium for recommending such an appointment/transfer. However, on account of propriety and judicial disciple I refrain from divulging these reasons," he wrote.
 
Citing another instance, Gavai alleged that a judge who had been transferred from his parent high court to another high court on punitive considerations was subsequently appointed chief justice of a large and prominent high court.
 
"In another instance, a judge was transferred from his parent high court to another high court on punitive consideration and was subsequently rewarded by appointment as chief justice of a large and a prominent high court," the letter read.

Gavai urges President to intervene

Gavai also questioned whether the Collegium's primacy in judicial appointments could place it beyond accountability.
 
Referring to Article 124(2) of the Constitution, which provides for the appointment of Supreme Court judges by the President, he argued that the President's constitutional responsibilities remained relevant to the process.
 
He said the Collegium's recommendations being treated as decisive under judicial convention did not make the body unaccountable or absolve the President of her constitutional duties.
 
Gavai also said the executive and Parliament were stakeholders in judicial appointments and transfers. He referred to instances in which the government and legislature had requested the Collegium and high courts to consider suitable candidates from marginalised communities to improve representation.
 
He urged President Murmu to intervene, as she deemed appropriate, and remind all stakeholders of their constitutional responsibilities towards ensuring equal representation in the higher judiciary.

data.title: Pet insurance explained: What is covered and why claims may get rejected
data.description:
Pet insurance can help owners manage the cost of unexpected veterinary treatment, including hospitalisation, surgery, diagnostic tests and medicines. But paying a premium does not mean every veterinary bill will be reimbursed. Waiting periods, pre-existing conditions, treatment-specific caps, co-payments and exclusions can significantly reduce the payout.
 
The actual value of a pet insurance policy depends not just on the sum insured but also on how much of a particular treatment the insurer agrees to cover.
 

What does pet insurance cover?

 
Pet insurance policies in India can cover expenses arising from illnesses and accidents, including veterinary consultations, diagnostic tests, prescribed medicines, hospitalisation and surgeries. Depending on the insurer and the policy selected, coverage may extend to outpatient department (OPD) treatment, dental care, specialised therapies, emergency ambulance services and third-party liability.
 
 
Ashwini Dubey, business head – home and pet insurance at Policybazaar, said some policies also offer benefits such as pet boarding, teleconsultations, death or loss benefits, trip cancellation, behavioural treatment and eligible pregnancy complications. However, these benefits may require separate covers or add-ons.
 
The extent of coverage can make a difference when an unexpected medical emergency arises.
 
Dubey shared three claim examples. In one case, a pet suffering from blood in the urine and stomach discomfort underwent investigations and kidney stone surgery, for which the insurer paid ₹42,991. In another, an accidental fall led to Grade 2 medial patellar luxation (MPL), requiring orthopaedic surgery, with a claim payout of ₹59,237.
 
In a third case, a pet swallowed a finger ring and required medical intervention, resulting in a claim payout of ₹35,390.
 
Arti Mulik, chief technical officer at Universal Sompo General Insurance, said hospitalisation expenses can range from ₹1,000 to ₹50,000, depending on the severity of the condition, while surgeries could cost even more.
 

What is not covered, and why can claims be rejected?

 
Pet insurance is designed to protect against unforeseen expenses rather than existing illnesses or predictable routine costs.
 
Mulik said common exclusions include pre-existing illnesses, cosmetic procedures, treatment by unqualified persons, conditions arising from deliberate neglect and government-banned breeds. Routine check-ups and vaccinations may be covered under specific plans or add-ons. Most policies also have waiting periods of 30 to 90 days, depending on the product.
 
Girish Sehgal, chief – health underwriting, claims, customer service and operations at ICICI Lombard, said the insurer's Paw Care policy generally excludes pre-existing conditions, subject to applicable continuity provisions. Claims arising during the initial 30-day waiting period are also excluded, except those resulting from accidents.
 
Routine expenses such as vaccinations, grooming, bathing and nail clipping are not covered under the general policy terms. Certain claims may also become inadmissible if prescribed preventive medicines or vaccinations have not been taken.
 
Owners should also check whether OPD treatment is covered, as consultations, diagnostic tests and medicines may not qualify under the base policy.
 

Why may the sum insured not be enough?

 
A policy offering ₹1 lakh in cover does not necessarily reimburse ₹1 lakh for every treatment. Treatment-specific sub-limits, deductibles and co-payments can reduce the payout.
 
Dubey illustrated this with an example of a minor illness claim under HDFC ERGO's Make Your Own Plan, which is capped at 25 per cent of the applicable illness sum insured or ₹15,000, whichever is lower. If the illness sum insured is ₹40,000, the maximum payout under this limit would be ₹10,000, even if the veterinary bill is ₹40,000.
 
Mulik said the premium should not be the sole criterion for buying insurance. Consider two owners who insure similar dogs for ₹25,000. One policy has no co-payment and higher surgery limits, while another offers a lower premium but imposes a 20 per cent co-payment and a surgery cap of ₹10,000.
 
For a ₹15,000 surgery, the second policy could pay less than ₹10,000 because of its sub-limit, despite the owner having paid premiums regularly.
 

What should pet owners check before buying insurance?

 
Sehgal advised pet owners to examine the sum insured, treatment-specific sub-limits, deductibles, co-payments, waiting periods, exclusions and age- and breed-based eligibility.
 
Dubey said owners should also check renewal conditions, premium revisions, claim-intimation timelines, cashless veterinary hospital availability, pre-authorisation requirements and claim-processing timelines.
 
Before purchasing, owners should disclose the pet's medical history, check vaccination requirements and understand whether coverage can continue as the pet ages.
 
While filing a claim, they should notify the insurer within the prescribed timeline, retain prescriptions, diagnosis reports and itemised bills, and ensure the pet's identification matches the policy.
 
Pet insurance is a financial protection tool against unexpected medical expenses, not a guarantee that every veterinary bill will be paid. Reading the policy wording before purchasing can help owners avoid unpleasant surprises when their pet needs treatment.

data.title: Global brands move Bangladesh orders worth millions to India amid unrest
data.description:
Global fashion retailers including Zara and H&M shifted nearly a tenth of their monthly orders from Bangladesh to other Asian manufacturing hubs in the first half of November, as labour unrest disrupted production and rising costs eroded the country's competitive edge, three factory owners said.
 
Between November 1 and 18, brands diverted about $254 million worth of orders from Bangladesh, with most moving to neighbouring India, the owners said, in a shift that represents a major blow to a key pillar of Bangladesh's economy and could extend beyond the current unrest.
 
Industry leaders have said rising wages, energy ‌shortages and political uncertainty have weakened the low-cost advantage that helped make Bangladesh the world's second-largest ​apparel exporter after China, prompting global brands to diversify sourcing.
  
The protests have caused ​more than $400 million in production losses, according to the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), in an industry that accounts for more than 80% of Bangladesh's export earnings and nearly 40% ​of its manufacturing jobs.
 
India has emerged as the biggest beneficiary of the order diversions, while buyers are also looking to Vietnam, Cambodia and Indonesia to reduce supply-chain risks and improve delivery reliability, industry leaders said.
 
Those pressures intensified on Wednesday when Bangladesh approved a 36% increase in the minimum wage for garment workers, though the rise was the smallest in four decades.
 
The increase fell well short of workers' demands to more than double wages, triggering fresh clashes with police even as Abdur Rahman Tarafder, secretary of the Ministry of Labour and Employment, said the wage increase was "satisfactory" ​and that he hoped all garment workers would resume work from Saturday.
 
Industry leaders said the increase would nevertheless narrow Bangladesh's labour-cost advantage over India, although union groups argue the wages remain low by global apparel ‌industry standards.
 
The factory owners, speaking on condition of anonymity because of concerns about their relationships with international buyers, said the unrest had prompted Zara, H&M, Marks & Spencer, Celio and ​other global brands to divert orders, with India receiving the bulk of the business.
 
Zara owner Inditex declined to comment on Reuters' questions, while M&S, H&M and Celio did not respond to requests for comment.
 
M. Mohiuddin Chowdhury, a director of the BGMEA, said higher wages, utility and raw-material costs were adding to pressure on manufacturers.
 
"The wage increase has added to costs at a time when buyers are demanding lower prices and competition ‌from rival sourcing countries is intensifying," he said.
 
Mahmud Hasan Khan, the group's ​president, declined to name the brands but said temporarily shifting some orders elsewhere helps the industry ‌retain global clients while minimising financial losses.
 
MORE BUSINESS AT RISK 
 
Factory owners said the bigger concern was that orders already diverted could be followed by the loss of future business as ‌buyers reassessed where to source garments.
 
Persistent energy shortages, exacerbated by the Middle East crisis, have added to production disruptions and forced some factories to rely on more expensive alternative power ​sources.
 
Chowdhury said buyers were increasingly prioritising delivery times over price when choosing suppliers.
 
"Price becomes secondary when brands are under pressure to meet strict delivery deadlines," he said.
 
India can offer buyers a delivery advantage of about a week, while Vietnam and Cambodia can cut lead times by as ​much as 15 days, Chowdhury said.
 
Rival sourcing hubs can typically complete production and delivery within 60 to 90 days, compared with about 120 days in Bangladesh, he added.
 
The disruptions have also created production backlogs, with manufacturers around Dhaka losing an estimated 20 to 25 production days. Some are considering overtime and costly air freight to meet ‌delivery commitments.
 
Khan Monirul Alam, managing director of Alps Apparels Group, which mainly supplies European brands, said the unrest was already hitting new business.
 
"Since November 1, most of my buyers have stopped ‌placing orders because of the unrest," Alam said. "They are telling us our orders have been shifted, postponed or cancelled and that they have already found alternative solutions."
 
Political tensions surrounding former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's possible return to Dhaka from India have added to concerns about further disruption.
 
Industry leaders said restoring stability and uninterrupted production would be critical to retaining international buyers. Chowdhury warned that orders shifted elsewhere during periods of instability might not return even after conditions improved.
 
"The challenge is restoring buyers' confidence before temporary shifts become long-term sourcing decisions," he said. "Brands have options. They will not wait for us ​if instability persists."

data.title: Sebi clarifies no change proposed to managing director age limit at MIIs
data.description:
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) on Friday clarified that its consultation paper on strengthening governance of market infrastructure institutions (MIIs) does not propose any change to the maximum age limit of 65 years for their managing directors (MDs). MIIs include stock exchanges, depositories, and clearing corporations. The regulator said that the proposals floated on November 20 regarding MDs concern only their term and tenure within a single MII and across MIIs. Incumbent public interest directors, MDs, and executive directors would continue till the end of their ongoing terms.
 
Sebi has proposed that a single term for a managing director (MD) would not exceed five years, with a maximum of two terms and eight years in one MII.
 
 
The proposed changes include lower age and term limits for public interest directors (PIDs), a 12-year cap on the combined tenure of managing directors across MIIs, and a board seat for the Association of Mutual Funds in India’s (Amfi’s) chief executive at the repo clearing corporation.
 
The regulator has proposed cutting the maximum age of PIDs from 75 to 70 years and the cap on terms from three to two. A PID would serve two terms of three years each across MIIs.
 
The regulator said the role is quasi-regulatory and more demanding than that of an ordinary non-executive director, and that a narrow pool of individuals can circulate between MIIs.

data.title: Britannia Industries CMO Puneet Das quits within 10 months of joining
data.description:
Leading bakery foods company Britannia Industries on Friday said its Chief Marketing Officer, Puneet Das, has resigned to pursue an opportunity outside the organisation, according to a regulatory filing.

Das, who joined Britannia in February 2026, will be relieved from the company's services with effect from the close of business on December 9, 2026, according to a regulatory filing.

"Puneet Das, Chief Marketing Officer, has decided to pursue an opportunity outside Britannia and has resigned from the services of the Company," said Britannia.

Das was appointed Chief Marketing Officer of Britannia Industries effective February 16, 2026. His exit comes less than 10 months after taking charge of the marketing function at the biscuit and bakery major.

data.title: India's power sector needs ₹200 trillion investments by 2047: Manohar Lal
data.description:
India's power sector will need investments to the tune of ₹200 trillion until 2047 to achieve various targets, Union minister Manohar Lal said on Friday, and called for stock market listings of state-owned firms and participation from private players to raise funds.

Speaking at the Power Ministers' Conference of States and Union Territories here, Lal emphasised the need for the Centre and states to work as a team to tackle challenges related to transmission of renewable energy.

The power minster also said that the total loss of discoms across the country has reached ₹7 trillion again, even after the central government absorbed about the same amount of losses in 2017 through UDAY (Ujjwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana), a financial package scheme for revival of power distribution companies (discoms).

 

"We absorbed about ₹7 trillion loss under the UDAY scheme in 2017. Losses of discoms of the entire nation have again reached ₹7 trillion," he said.

He also pointed out that last year, all discoms together earned a profit of ₹2,600 crore.

Now the challenge is that we should not turn this profit into a loss again, he said and suggested the states to use these profits to set off losses incurred earlier.

"We need to ensure that the financial position of our DISCOMs is strengthened and necessary changes in policy, operations and regulation should facilitate the continuation of this turnaround," he said.

About the investment opportunity in the power sector, he said, "There will be investment of ₹200 trillion to meet fixed targets in the power sector only by 2047, which is equal to five years' budget of the government. We cannot do this investment alone. We need investments from the public and list our public sector firms as well as investment of private sector under the public-private partnership." Prime Minister Narendra Modi has recently stated that 500 GW more renewable energy would be added in the next 10 years.

Today we have 300 GW of installed renewable energy capacity, he noted.

For expanding the power transmission network, the Centre and states would need to work as 'Team India', he said, as he highlighted the lack of transmission network, especially for renewable energy, and said there is problem or issues in evacuation of solar power.

It is not a good situation that there is huge generation of power but there is a lack of transmission network to evacuate that, he said.

He further said that the power demand will increase due to expanding data centre infrastructure and increased usage of electric vehicles.

There is a need to focus on storage for optimum use of solar and other renewable sources, he said and urged states to encourage use of solar energy for agriculture and generation of electricity through rooftop solar.

He also highlighted that there are shortcomings in tariff, coordination and regulation (of tariff) of renewable energy sources, saying the regulation should be such that the discoms should not suffer losses.

The minister invited suggestions to add energy storage capacities, advocated the use of advanced technologies like pre-paid smart meters and AI tools to improve delivery, and asked states to clear pending electricity bills of government establishments and official residences to set the precedent.

He also asked states to focus on nuclear power for clean source of energy for the future.

The two-day power conference began on Friday. The last such conference at the national level was held in 2024.

According to a power ministry statement, the conference will comprise interactions and in-depth discussions among the Ministry of Power, states and other stakeholders on key issues such as implementation of resource adequacy plans, including accelerated energy storage deployment; inter-state and intra-state transmission issues; financial viability of discoms, implementation of the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), with emphasis on smart metering, feeder separation and household electrification; and issues related to nuclear sites.

Shripad Yesso Naik, Minister of State for Power, asked the participating states and UTs to share their experiences, including difficulties in implementation, regulatory issues and areas where further support or intervention from the central government may be required.

"Our collective focus should be on moving from policy formulation to effective execution, from infrastructure creation to measurable outcomes, and from individual interventions to an integrated and sustainable power sector", Naik said.

Power Secretary Pankaj Agarwal noted that the core guidance received from the Prime Minister is to move beyond energy security toward true energy independence in service of Viksit Bharat@2047.

The past year has been one of record growth, he said, and noted that India's installed capacity is now about 563 GW, and more than 55 per cent of it is non-fossil.

In the last 12 months, around 60 GW of capacity was added, 87 per cent of it from non-fossil sources, he said.

On November 28, the conference will have a joint session with the Forum of Regulators and State Electricity Regulatory Commissions (SERCs).

data.title: Vivo X500 series launched in India: Check specs, price details, and more
data.description:
Vivo has launched its X500 series smartphones in India, introducing three models: the X500, X500 Pro and X500 Pro Max. The new flagship line-up, co-engineered with ZEISS, puts the focus on photography and videography, with features such as telephoto autofocus tracking. The X500 Pro Max leads the range with a 200MP ZEISS APO telephoto camera and support for an optional 400mm equivalent teleconverter.
 
All three smartphones run Android 17-based OriginOS 7 and are powered by MediaTek Dimensity 9600-series chipsets. While the X500 Pro Max and X500 Pro use the Dimensity 9600 Pro, the standard X500 is powered by the Dimensity 9600M.
 

Vivo X500 series: Price and availability

The Vivo X500 series is available for pre-booking in India, with open sales scheduled to begin on December 3. The smartphones are available through Flipkart, Amazon, Vivo India's online store and authorised retail outlets.
 
The prices of the three smartphones are as follows:
 
Vivo X500
  • 12GB RAM + 256GB storage: Rs 119,999
Vivo X500 Pro
  • 12GB RAM + 256GB storage: Rs 149,999
Vivo X500 Pro Max
  • 12GB RAM + 256GB storage: Rs 164,999
  • 12GB RAM + 512GB storage: Rs 179,999
Accessories available for separate purchase:
  • 400 mm Equivalent vivo ZEISS Telephoto Extender Gen 2 Ultra: Rs 27,999
  • 200 mm Equivalent vivo ZEISS Telephoto Extender Gen 2: Rs 15,999
  • Imaging Grip Kit: Rs 11,999
  • Phone Strap: Rs 2,699
  • Magnetic Case: Rs 1,499(X500 Pro Max and X500 Pro), Rs 1,399(X500)
Customers can also get the 12GB RAM + 512GB storage variant of the Vivo X500 Pro Max with the Photography Kit at Rs 2,29,999. It includes the smartphone, a 200mm equivalent ZEISS Telephoto Extender Gen 2, a 400mm equivalent ZEISS Telephoto Extender Gen 2 Ultra and a shoulder strap.
ALSO READ: Apple may launch five Product(RED) edition devices on Dec 1: What to expect
It should be noted that Vivo's ZEISS teleconverter accessories are not universally compatible across the X500 series. The 200mm equivalent ZEISS Telephoto Extender Gen 2 is compatible with all three smartphones. The 400mm equivalent ZEISS Telephoto Extender Gen 2 Ultra, on the other hand, is designed exclusively for the X500 Pro Max. The Vivo Imaging Grip Kit is also exclusive to the X500 Pro Max.

Vivo X500 series: Launch offers

As part of the launch offers, buyers can avail up to 10 per cent cashback on eligible bank cards and UPI transactions, or a 10 per cent upgrade and exchange bonus. The exchange bonus cannot be combined with cashback or no-cost EMI offers. Vivo is also offering up to 24 months of no-cost EMI on eligible purchases.
ALSO READ: Croma Black Friday sale: Check offers on iPhones, MacBook Neo and more
Additional benefits include three months of Google AI Pro access with 5TB of cloud storage and 12 months of Canva Pro with an eligible Jio recharge of Rs 399.

Vivo X500 series specifications

Vivo X500 specifications:
  • Display: 6.59-inch 1.5K AMOLED display with 144Hz refresh rate
  • Processor: MediaTek Dimensity 9600M
  • Rear cameras: 50MP primary, 50MP ultra-wide and 64MP telephoto
  • Front camera: 50MP
  • RAM and storage: 12GB RAM + 256GB storage
  • Battery: 7,500mAh
  • Charging: 90W wired and 40W wireless charging
  • Operating system: Android 17-based OriginOS 7
  • Water and dust resistance: IP68 and IP69
Vivo X500 Pro specifications:
  • Display: 6.36-inch 1.5K AMOLED display with 144Hz refresh rate
  • Processor: MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro
  • Rear cameras: 50MP primary, 50MP ultra-wide and 64MP periscope telephoto
  • Front camera: 50MP
  • RAM and storage: 12GB RAM + 256GB storage
  • Battery: 6,510mAh
  • Charging: 90W wired and 40W wireless charging
  • Operating system: Android 17-based OriginOS 7
  • Water and dust resistance: IP68 and IP69
Vivo X500 Pro Max specifications:
  • Display: 6.85-inch 2K ZEISS Master Color LTPO AMOLED display with 144Hz refresh rate
  • Processor: MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro
  • Rear cameras: 50MP primary, 50MP ultra-wide and 200MP ZEISS APO telephoto
  • Front camera: 50MP

data.title: Karthigai Deepam row: SC issues contempt notice to Tamil Nadu officials
data.description:
Observing that the executive authorities in Tamil Nadu acted on the diktat of their political bosses, the Supreme Court on Friday issued a contempt notice to the Tamil Nadu chief secretary, DGP, Madurai collector and others over the violation of its November 20 Karthigai Deepam order.

The top court suspended the board of trustees of Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple and ordered lighting of lamp at Thiruparankundram Deepathoon on Saturday using the flame lit at Uchaipillaiyar mandapam.

Asking the Tamil Nadu chief secretary to appear personally, a bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi directed him to file an affidavit detailing emails, calls exchanged and messages exchanged between officials.

 

"The wilful non-compliance of orders of the Court, especially by the executive authorities, cannot go unnoticed and it has to be dealt with an iron hand," the bench said.

The top court also handed over the security of Tamil Nadu's Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple and Thiruparankundram hill to CRPF, citing the failure of the Tamil Nadu Police to implement its orders.

The apex court said it cannot sit in a silo if its order is not complied with and added that its order is not an invitation to negotiate as it binds the State, its officers and every religious institution.

It said any attempt to pollute stream of justice by any person, howsoever high he may be, will not be tolerated.

The top court said the conduct of officers prima facie reveals a state of administrative chaos in Tamil Nadu.

"The conduct alleged, as borne out by the record, would prima facie disclose a brazen and wilful disobedience of this Court's order, a flagrant disregard of the undertaking given before the High Court and a calculated affront to the authority of both constitutional courts," the bench said.

On Wednesday, the Tamil Nadu government apologised to the top court over the non-lighting of the ceremonial lamp at Deepathoon and blamed the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple authorities for it.

Despite the apex court's permission, the Karthigai Deepam was lit only at its customary Uchipillayar mandapam at Thirupparankundram on November 24 and not at Deepathoon.

data.title: Bangladesh minister says Hasina is a 'thorn' in bilateral ties with India
data.description:
Sheikh Hasina has become a "thorn" in Bangladesh-India relations, with New Delhi beginning to realise the strain her presence in the country is causing to bilateral ties, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir has said.

Comparing the deposed prime minister to an unwelcome guest who suddenly walks into someone's home, Kobir said India is in a difficult position as it could neither send her away nor avoid dealing with her presence, news portal bdnews24 reported.

"Hasina has become a thorn in Bangladesh-India relations," he told reporters at the foreign ministry on Thursday.

"She has become an irritation, and they understand that this is a problem for the relationship," Kobir said.

 

His remarks came a day after India refrained from commenting on Hasina's plan to return to Bangladesh on December 16.

External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal on Wednesday said that her voluntary return should be treated separately from Dhaka's extradition request, which New Delhi is examining through established legal processes.

Kobir reiterated that Hasina could return only under the extradition treaty between India and Bangladesh, either in handcuffs or under strict surveillance.

"She is a criminal. There is one policy for criminals and another for ordinary citizens. She falls under the criminal category. She will come only through the extradition treaty. It is not a matter of her returning; she will be handed over," he said.

Hasina's presence in India has emerged as a contentious issue in bilateral ties since her departure from Bangladesh.

She faces serious legal challenges in her home country, including a death sentence handed down in absentia by a special tribunal over the deadly crackdown on protesters during the uprising in 2024.

Hasina has denied wrongdoing and questioned the legitimacy of the proceedings.

Her spokesperson Syed Mozammel Ali on Tuesday said that the 79-year-old ousted premier plans to return home on December 16, the day the country celebrates its victory over Pakistan in the 1971 Liberation War.

Hasina, the daughter of Bangladesh's founding leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, ruled the country for 15 years before her ouster.

India had enjoyed close relations with Hasina during her 15 years in power and hoped that the formation of a new government in Bangladesh would provide an opportunity to reset ties, which deteriorated sharply after her ouster.

However, since taking office in February, Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman is yet to visit India despite an invitation. He skipped the BRICS summit hosted by India in September.

data.title: Vivo X500 Pro Max first impressions: Premium phone built around photography
data.description:
The Vivo X500 Pro Max is not a smartphone that blends into the crowd. From its large circular camera module to its sizeable display, the device makes its intentions clear. It is designed for users who place photography high on their list of priorities, and Vivo has gone a step further by offering optional teleconverter attachments to extend its imaging capabilities. Having spent some time with the device, its design, in-hand feel and display have made a good first impression.
 
Starting with the design, the Vivo X500 Pro Max retains the circular camera arrangement seen on its predecessor. However, the company has made some changes to the rear panel. The upper portion of the glass back, which houses the camera module, is slightly raised and slopes gently into the rest of the panel. This gives the phone a distinctive appearance without making the camera housing feel like an entirely separate component.
 
 
The aluminium frame adds to the construction, while the glass back has a smooth finish with a subtle pattern. It does attract fingerprints, though. The phone is available in Apex Orange and Eternal Black colour options, with different finishes on the rear panel.
ALSO READ: Vivo X500 series launched in India: Check specs, price details, and more
Despite its sizeable camera hardware, the X500 Pro Max measures between 7.95mm and 8.12mm in thickness, depending on the colour variant, and weighs 225g or 229g. It is not a lightweight smartphone, but the weight distribution makes it reasonably comfortable to hold. The index finger naturally rests below the camera module, which also helps when holding the phone in landscape orientation for photography. However, its large footprint means two-handed operation is often more convenient.
 
The camera system is where Vivo wants the X500 Pro Max to distinguish itself. The phone features a 50MP primary camera, a 50MP ultra-wide camera and a 200MP ZEISS APO telephoto camera. The latter has an 85mm equivalent focal length and is the centrepiece of the setup.
 
Vivo is also offering optional teleconverter attachments to extend the phone's photography capabilities. The range includes a 200mm equivalent ZEISS Telephoto Extender Gen 2 and a 400mm equivalent Gen 2 Ultra. There is also an Imaging Grip Kit with a physical shutter button and zoom dial. Together, these accessories make the phone resemble a compact camera setup and are aimed at users interested in wildlife and long-distance photography.
 
Moving to the front, the X500 Pro Max features a 6.85-inch 2K ZEISS Master Color AMOLED display with a 144Hz refresh rate. The panel has narrow, symmetrical bezels and a flat design, while a small punch-hole houses the front camera. The screen looks sharp, with deep blacks and vibrant colours.
ALSO READ: GTA 6 India launch: First impressions, prices, editions and download size
The LTPO panel can dynamically switch its refresh rate between 1Hz and 144Hz, depending on the content. Vivo claims peak brightness of up to 5,000 nits, while the high-brightness mode is rated at 2,000 nits. The display also supports Dolby Vision and HDR10+, while an ultrasonic fingerprint sensor is embedded underneath.
 
The Vivo X500 Pro Max makes a good first impression with its design, in-hand feel and AMOLED display. The teleconverter attachments also give it a different proposition from conventional flagship smartphones. However, their usefulness and the extent to which they improve the photography experience need closer examination.
 
There is still more to assess, including camera performance across different conditions, processing capabilities, software and battery life. The full review of the Vivo X500 Pro Max will be out soon.

Vivo X500 Pro Max: Price and availability

The smartphone is available for pre-booking in India, with open sales scheduled to begin on December 3.
  • 12GB RAM + 256GB storage: Rs 164,999
  • 12GB RAM + 512GB storage: Rs 179,999
Accessories available for separate purchase:
  • 400 mm Equivalent vivo ZEISS Telephoto Extender Gen 2 Ultra: Rs 27,999
  • 200 mm Equivalent vivo ZEISS Telephoto Extender Gen 2: Rs 15,999
  • Imaging Grip Kit: Rs 11,999
  • Phone Strap: Rs 2,699
  • Magnetic Case: Rs 1,499 (X500 Pro Max and X500 Pro)
Customers can also get the 12GB RAM + 512GB storage variant of the Vivo X500 Pro Max with the Photography Kit at Rs 229,999. It includes the smartphone, a 200mm equivalent ZEISS Telephoto Extender Gen 2, a 400mm equivalent ZEISS Telephoto Extender Gen 2 Ultra and a shoulder strap.
